keyVerseText: Whether it be in the warp, or woof; of linen, or of woollen; whether in a skin, or in any thing made of skin; thing: Heb. work of
rootMeaning: The root of שְׁתִי (shᵉthîy) derives from the verb שִׁית (shîyth), which broadly means to place, set, or appoint. This etymology highlights the concept of something being deliberately arranged or fixed in position. In the case of שְׁתִי, it specifically refers to the warp—the set of threads stretched lengthwise on a loom—emphasizing the foundational and ordered aspect of the woven material rather than a random or incidental part. This root sense enriches our understanding beyond the English gloss by underscoring intentionality and structure inherent in the warp.
usageInScripture: The word שְׁתִי appears nine times in Scripture, consistently referring to the warp in weaving. Translations vary slightly but maintain a focus on the warp, with phrases such as 'either in the warp,' 'in the warp,' and 'whether it be in the warp' dominating usage. This consistency reveals the term's specialized meaning related to the textile craft, specifically the longitudinal threads that provide the framework through which the woof is woven. The word’s use is technical and precise, underscoring its role in describing the fabric’s essential structure.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שְׁתִי as the warp—the fixed, foundational threads in weaving—invites reflection on God’s providential ordering in creation and redemption. Just as the warp holds the fabric together, God’s sovereign will and covenantal purposes provide the unchanging framework within which the story of redemption unfolds. This imagery can remind believers that though the details of life may vary (the woof), God's purposes remain steadfast and secure. It also points to the interconnectedness and unity God weaves into His people and His promises, calling believers to trust in the divine design that holds all things together in Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 13:48 states, 'Whether it be in the warp, or woof; of linen, or of woollen; whether in a skin, or in any thing made of skin.' Here, שְׁתִי (warp) highlights the precise location within a fabric that might be affected by a condition, emphasizing the thoroughness of the law’s concern with purity and holiness. The term’s meaning as the lengthwise threads underlines the foundational aspect of what is being examined, symbolizing how even the most basic and integral parts of life and worship must be set apart for God. This careful distinction reminds believers of the call to holiness in every aspect of their lives.
